symptom: The standalone synthetic signature-claim and reference-anchor snapshots checked toJSON membership on the caller's live Proxy before copying own data descriptors. A has trap could replace an initially invalid Ed25519 signature with the matching signature, or change a revoked reference to ACTIVE, before the snapshot; the later deny-only consistency flag could then become true. No independent authentication or scoring was granted.
lesson: Snapshotting before signature math is insufficient if the snapshot helper itself runs a live membership trap before reading the descriptors. An apparently harmless toJSON check can mutate the very signature or reference status that is about to be copied.
guardrail: Do not perform toJSON membership checks on untrusted claim/reference Proxies before copying own descriptors. Preserve exact own-key admission, reject inherited toJSON via the known built-in prototype only, and test that live has traps never execute while invalid signatures and revoked references remain denied. These are caller-supplied synthetic metadata, not independent trust roots; independentAuthorityVerified and scoringAuthorized stay false.
